newsitem.title: UK: Gallaher sets date for stockmarket debut.
newsitem.headline: Gallaher sets date for stockmarket debut.

text.p: British tobacco group Gallaher said on Friday it plans to list on the London stockmarket on May 30 after its demerger from American Brands Inc.

Gallaher controls 39 percent of the British tobacco market, owning the Benson and Hedges and Silk Cut brands. Although the company did not disclose an anticipated share price for its listing, analysts expect the company to be valued at about 2.2 billion pounds with a share price of around 320p.
The company said Canadian and American residents who hold American Brands stock prior to May 30 will receive one Gallaher ADS for every one American Brands share.

Each Gallaher ADS will represent four Gallaher ordinary shares. All other holders of American Brands common stock will receive four Gallaher ordinary shares for every one share of American Brands stock.

"The demerger will allow Gallaher to focus its financial and management resources on enhancing its products, developing new markets and products and expanding its business outside the United Kingdom," said Peter Wilson chairman and chief executive.

In 1996 Gallaher showed turnover of 4.37 billion pounds ($7.2 billion) of which 86 percent came from Britain where it is the largest manufacturer of tobacco products. The group reported total trading profit of 361.5 million pounds.
Most of its business in Britain comes from the sale of cigarettes, mainly in the premium sector, but it also sells Hamlet cigars, Condor pipe tobacco and Old Holborn hand rolling tobacco.
Benson and Hedges is Britain's largest-selling cigarette brand while Silk Cut is the largest selling low-tar cigarette.
Gallaher also has an increasing share of the growing low-priced sector through its Mayfair and Sovereign brands.

The company makes cigarettes and pipe and handrolling tobacco in Lisnafillan in Northern Ireland, cigarettes in Hyde, near Manchester and in Dublin and cigars in Cardiff. It plans to expand its Lisnafillan plant and close the Hyde factory over the next three to four years.
